suggestions.title: Last call: step on the scale tomorrow morning — the fat-or-water verdict dies with it

rationale.science: Scale weight is noisy day to day — water, sodium and glycogen swing it without any fat change (Powers 2003) — which is exactly why one morning read against a carried trend is enough: a single number grades a two-week question that no amount of waiting can.
rationale.data: Last read 8/21 at 162.4; trend carried at 162.9 for ten days; your measured rate currently reads anywhere from standing still to ~0.74 lb/wk — an interval your own app now prints too.
rationale.relationship: One read collapses that interval and grades the late-August drop: mid-162s means fat, confirmed; low 163s means water giveback, on script; above 163.5 means I over-read it. Tomorrow is the deadline I set — after that the verdict files unanswered.

suggestions.predict: A read tomorrow lands mid-162s (162.2–163.1) and the verdict files as fat. If the morning passes blank, the verdict files unanswered tomorrow night — no penalty, but the claim dies untested. If it lands above 163.5, I over-read the whoosh and will say so in the next brief.

suggestions.title: Four days left in the free layoff — log sessions if any happened, or write "rest week" and make it a planned deload

rationale.science: Trained lifters give back essentially nothing in the first ~2 weeks away, and what little goes returns fast (Mujika & Padilla 2000, detraining review). Past that window, real strength and size start to go.
rationale.data: Last logged session 8/21 — hack squat 200 × 8,7,8 and the hip thrust machine's first outing. Today is day ten. The window closes about Friday.
rationale.relationship: A one-line entry decides which story this is: a planned deload inside the free window, or an unplanned slide past it. Either way the comeback opens at 1–2 reps in reserve against your 8/21 baselines — declines assumed nowhere.

suggestions.predict: A session or a rest-week line lands by Friday and the layoff files as cheap, comeback starting from your existing baselines. If the file stays dark past Friday, the next briefs start pricing real strength cost — and next weekend's brief becomes a comeback plan, as promised.

suggestions.title: Log today's food — forward only, no reconstructing last week

rationale.science: Food recalled days later runs badly under-reported — it's the norm, not the exception (Lichtman 1992) — and adherence gaps, not metabolism, explain most stalls (Alhassan 2008). Fresh entries are trustworthy; reconstructed ones aren't.
rationale.data: No food logged since 8/20 — eleven days. On Sunday your app re-checked its maintenance estimate and wrote the same number it had Friday: nothing new to chew on.
rationale.relationship: The maintenance math behind your calorie band only learns from matched days — food beside a morning weight. Every fresh logged day feeds it; guessed back-fill poisons it. The band stays the app's call; the job here is just feeding it true days.

suggestions.predict: The first matched day lands and the maintenance estimate starts moving again within a couple of updates. If matched days return and it stays frozen anyway, my read of how it learns is wrong and I'll say so. If no food lands this week, this card rides until it does.
